subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should hosted skill publishes preserve these source flags as visibly unverified attribution, deprecate them as unsupported metadata, or use them to initiate server-side verification?
rationale: The existing trusted-provenance boundary is intentional, but current code and documentation do not define the permanent retention and visibility contract; choosing one changes the registry trust model and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Expose Unverified Attribution
options.body: Persist and display the declared repository and commit under a clearly unverified field excluded from verification, trust badges, and install decisions.

options.title: Deprecate The Flags
options.body: Warn and eventually reject these flags for hosted skill publishes, directing publishers to the server-managed GitHub-backed workflow for trusted provenance.

options.title: Verify Before Trust
options.body: Add repository authorization and uploaded-content matching before storing a CLI claim as trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Expose Unverified Attribution
recommendation.body: Persist and display the declared repository and commit under a clearly unverified field excluded from verification, trust badges, and install decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged GitHub-backed source work is the strongest feature-history signal for deciding how hosted publishes should relate to trusted source-backed skills.
